Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

memoria

memoria, memoriae f.

noun, first declension

memory, the power of remembering; the memory of something, remembrance

In this lexicon

  • memory

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Brut. 301: memoria tanta quantam in nūllō cognōvisse mē arbitror; Quint. 1.3.1; Traupman 344

  • memory

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.105: suāvis labōrum est praeteritōrum memoria; Cic. Sen. 71

Examples

  • ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est. ejus duplex virtūs, facile percipere et fidēliter continēre

    in small children the chief sign of ability is memory, and its virtue is twofold: to take things in easily and to keep them faithfullyQuint. 1.3.1

    In the entry for memory

  • initia litterārum sōlā memoriā cōnstant, quae nōn modo jam est in parvīs sed tum etiam tenācissima est

    the first steps in learning rest on memory alone, which small children not only have already but have at its most retentiveQuint. 1.1.19

    In the entry for memory

  • tamen quid habuistis in cēnā? — dīcam, sī potuerō; nam tam bonae memoriae sum, ut frequenter nōmen meum oblīvīscar

    Still, what did you have for dinner? — I’ll tell you if I can; my memory is so good that I often forget my own name.Petr. 66.1
